+    return table
+
+
+def _apply_table(s, table):
+    """
+    s with every replacement of table (from _replace_table) applied in order.
+    A pair can only occur if both of its code points are in s, so replacements
+    whose tokens are absent are skipped (they would not change s); present is
+    a superset of the code points of s (a minted token is added once created).
+    """
+    present = set(s)
+    for a, b, ps, c in table:
+        if a in present and b in present:
+            n = len(s)
+            s = s.replace(ps, c)
+            if len(s) != n:
+                present.add(c)
+    return s

journal.text:
I tried to speed up encode in minbpe by reworking the cached state helpers in basic.py and regex.py (the _replace_table, _chunk_table and _enc_state paths). I added a block at the end of basic.py, then reverted most of it to a two line version, and made small matching edits in regex.py around lines 18, 29 and 311.

One sandbox evaluation on encode_ir was rejected for no improvement. Outputs were identical and the guard passed with 2 files and 34 lines. encode_ir went from 428615941 to 432679968, ratio 1.0095, against a required 0.9900. train_ir went from 370850212 to 371641112, ratio 1.0021. I stopped without submitting a candidate.

My belief now is that the existing table caching is already near what this approach can give. Shuffling where state lives only added overhead.

Next I should profile the encode inner loop directly, the merge lookup and the per-chunk pair scan, and look for an algorithmic change instead of moving caches around.
